reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected SEC exhibit rows shows a divergence between GAAP and company-defined adjusted measures that the selected rows do not reconcile. GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders and continuing-operations income decline sequentially and are equal to each other in both periods, while total adjusted pre-tax income, General Insurance adjusted pre-tax income and adjusted after-tax income attributable to common all increase. Consolidated net investment income falls while APTI-basis net investment income rises, so the two investment-income bases move in opposite directions; the selected rows do not identify the reconciling items between them. Within General Insurance, underwriting income rises and the reported combined ratio improves, but the company-defined accident-year loss ratio is unchanged and the accident-year combined ratio is essentially flat, indicating that the reported combined-ratio improvement is not explained by current-period accident-year loss experience in these rows. Gross and net premiums written both decline sequentially, which is consistent with a smaller premium base rather than with improved underlying loss trends, and the selected rows do not separate volume, rate, mix or cession effects. Other Operations adjusted pre-tax loss widens slightly. Because the GAAP-to-adjusted bridge, the investment-income basis difference and the drivers of the premium decline are not present in the selected rows, the direction of the underlying earnings trend cannot be established from this extract; the appropriate research state is a preserved hold pending reconciliation evidence rather than a conviction change. No causal attribution is asserted, and no valuation or trade conclusion is drawn.
